name: Sack of Baghdad
summary: Hulagu Khan's Mongol army sacks Baghdad over thirteen days in February 1258. The last Abbasid Caliph al-Musta'sim is executed (wrapped in a carpet and trampled by horses, according to tradition, to avoid shedding royal blood). The House of Wisdom, the greatest library in the medieval world, is destroyed; eyewitnesses describe the Tigris running black with ink. The event marks the definitive end of the Islamic Golden Age and is considered one of the most catastrophic in Islamic history.

_quarry.structural_significance: End of the Abbasid Caliphate (750–1258); destruction of Baghdad as a political and cultural center; Mamluks install a shadow Abbasid caliph in Cairo
